comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Measured, and it passes. tools/latency.py (./dev --latency): input-to-glyph over a plain PTY is 1.4 ms at the median, 22.6 ms at p95, at a typist's cadence. Full table and method in docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 9.

The tail is not double emulation. The daemon answers every keystroke in about 1 ms; in 23 of 60 samples the first frame did not yet carry the byte, because the PTY echo lost a race against a render already in flight, and the glyph then waited out herdr's 16 ms MIN_RENDER_INTERVAL (src/app/mod.rs:35, gated in App::can_render_now at src/app/runtime.rs:519). Roughly 1.4 ms or roughly 20 ms, with almost nothing between.

None of that is Muster's code - one render_and_stream serves every render target, so herdr's own TUI sits behind the same gate. What Muster adds is frame decode and VT parse, 5.96 and 3.72 ns/byte (./dev --perf): about 0.35 ms for a 35 KB repaint, microseconds for the diffs after it.

Method note worth keeping: the first version read frames on a second thread and reported a 20 ms median. The measuring loop held the GIL and starved the reader, so the number described the instrument. Single-threaded blocking reads took the median from 20 ms to 1.4 ms.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Daemon VT -> re-encoded ANSI -> surface VT. Measure keypress-to-glyph against plain ghostty. Stage-1 gate: must feel native.
title: Measure double-emulation latency
